Fix the parser so that an empty final line does not discard the previous record. Keep the existing return type and preserve the order of valid records. Add a focused regression test for a file that ends with two newline characters, then run the parser tests. Do not modify authentication, upgrade dependencies, or deploy anything. If the failure turns out to come from a different subsystem, explain that finding before expanding the change. Finish with a brief explanation of the cause and the exact checks that passed.

Fix the import parser that drops the final valid record when an uploaded file ends with an empty line. Start by reading the parser and the tests that exercise it. Reproduce the problem with a small local fixture before changing the implementation. The same file without the trailing blank line imports every record, so use that comparison to narrow down the cause. Keep the change focused on parsing and preserve the order in which valid records appeared in the source.

The input can use Unix or Windows line endings. A blank line at the end is allowed, and a blank line between records should continue to follow the existing behavior. A field containing spaces is not automatically an empty record. Do not trim field values, normalize quoted content, or replace the public return type. Existing callers expect the same error shape and the same record identifiers. Preserve those contracts even if a different interface would make the implementation shorter.

Add focused regression coverage for a single trailing newline, several trailing blank lines, Windows line endings, and a final record whose last field contains spaces. Reuse the existing fixture helpers rather than introducing a new testing library. Run the parser tests after the fix. If a test fails, read its actual failure and fix the cause before moving on. A broader suite is useful only if the change reaches code that the focused tests do not cover.

Do not modify authentication, update dependencies, migrate stored data, delete uploaded files, or deploy anything. Use synthetic input rather than downloading customer records. If the defect actually belongs to a different subsystem, stop before expanding the implementation and explain the evidence and the smallest proposed change. Keep unrelated work intact. When the parser fix is complete, summarize the original failure, explain how the new behavior handles the final record, list the checks that passed, and call out any behavior you could not verify. Do not claim success based only on reading the code.
